title: Aeroflot 3352
summary: A Tupolev Tu-154 descending to land at Omsk struck maintenance vehicles on the runway, killing all 178 people on board. The ground controller fell asleep on duty, failed to engage the runway-occupied warning, and incorrectly authorized runway maintenance. Poorly lit maintenance vehicles were invisible to the approaching pilots.
probable_cause: The aircraft struck maintenance vehicles on the runway due to the controller falling asleep, failing to implement required safety procedures, and inadequate vehicle lighting.

factors.evidence: The 23-year-old ground controller was inexperienced and had insufficient sleep in days before the accident.
Ground controller fell asleep and did not switch on the runway occupied warning.
Maintenance crew kept vehicle lights on only at start and finish, preventing pilots from seeing vehicles on runway.
Flight was approaching in poor weather with light rain and 3 km visibility with 100 m ceiling.
Aircraft struck three maintenance vehicles positioned on the runway at 5:36 a.m.

events.text: Maintenance crew requested permission to dry runway; ground controller gave permission then fell asleep and forgot to activate runway occupied warning.
Three maintenance vehicles moved to runway: UAZ-469 with trailer followed by KrAZ and Ural trucks.
Maintenance crew attempted to contact ground control three times about runway lights but received no response.
Flight 3352 requested permission to land; aircraft struck maintenance vehicles on runway at high speed.

notes: deadliest aviation accident on Russian territory at time
ground controller sentenced to 15 years, died by suicide in prison
